topics.name: Spring Boot vs Spring
topics.summary: See what Boot configures for a Spring application and which decisions still belong to you.

subTopics.name: Why Spring Boot was introduced
subTopics.summary: Boot makes it easier to bootstrap and run a Spring application with sensible defaults.

subTopics.name: Problems it solves
subTopics.summary: Use starters, conditional configuration, and embedded servers to reduce setup work.

subTopics.name: Spring vs Spring Boot (VERY COMMON)
subTopics.summary: Spring provides the framework. Boot packages conventions and automatic configuration around it.

topics.name: @SpringBootApplication
topics.summary: Understand what the main Boot annotation enables and where scanning starts.

subTopics.name: What it is internally
subTopics.summary: SpringBootApplication configures the application, enables auto-configuration, and starts component scanning.

subTopics.name: Combination of: @Configuration, @ComponentScan, @EnableAutoConfiguration
subTopics.summary: Its configuration role comes from SpringBootConfiguration, which is itself a Configuration annotation.

subTopics.name: Why it should be placed in root package
subTopics.summary: Place the application class above the packages you want scanned, or set the boundaries explicitly.

topics.name: Starters
topics.summary: Pick a starter to bring in a coordinated set of dependencies for one capability.

subTopics.name: What are starters?
subTopics.summary: A starter is a dependency descriptor for a common application feature.

subTopics.name: How spring-boot-starter-web works
subTopics.summary: The web starter brings together Spring MVC and related dependencies for a servlet web application.

subTopics.name: Why starters reduce dependency conflicts
subTopics.summary: Boot dependency management aligns supported library versions. Check overrides for compatibility.

topics.name: Configuration Management
topics.summary: Separate configuration from code and inspect which source wins.

subTopics.name: application.properties vs application.yml
subTopics.summary: Properties uses flat keys. YAML can group related keys in a nested document.

subTopics.name: YAML advantages
subTopics.summary: YAML makes nested configuration and lists easier to scan when indentation is consistent.

subTopics.name: Profile-specific files
subTopics.summary: Use application-profile files for values that apply only to an active profile.

subTopics.name: Profiles (Dev, QA, Prod)
subTopics.summary: Keep common defaults in the base config and put environment-specific values in appropriate sources.

subTopics.name: Externalized Configuration: Property Source Order
subTopics.summary: System properties can override OS variables, and OS variables can override config data. Command-line arguments can override these.

subTopics.name: How environment variables override config
subTopics.summary: Set a matching environment variable such as SERVER_PORT to override configuration from a file.

subTopics.name: @Value vs @ConfigurationProperties
subTopics.summary: Use Value for an individual value and ConfigurationProperties for a group of related settings.

subTopics.name: @Value vs @ConfigurationProperties - Differences and When to use which
subTopics.summary: Choose structured binding when several values belong together and need validation.

subTopics.name: Type safety advantages of @ConfigurationProperties
subTopics.summary: ConfigurationProperties converts values to declared types and can validate the result at startup.

topics.name: Developer Tools
topics.summary: Use development tools to shorten feedback cycles and know what your build generates.

subTopics.name: Spring Boot DevTools (Live Reload)
subTopics.summary: DevTools can restart on classpath changes and trigger browser reload when supported.

subTopics.name: Lombok integration
subTopics.summary: Lombok generates code during compilation. Align annotation processing in the IDE and build.

topics.name: Auto-Configuration Internals
topics.summary: Predict what Boot creates by reading the conditions on its auto-configuration.

subTopics.name: What is auto-configuration?
subTopics.summary: Boot supplies configuration when matching dependencies, properties, and application conditions are present.

subTopics.name: How Spring Boot decides which bean to create
subTopics.summary: Conditions evaluate available types, existing beans, and configuration before registering candidates.

subTopics.name: @ConditionalOnClass
subTopics.summary: OnClass makes a configuration conditional on the presence of specified types.

subTopics.name: @ConditionalOnMissingBean
subTopics.summary: OnMissingBean lets Boot provide a default when the application has not supplied a matching bean.

subTopics.name: @ConditionalOnProperty
subTopics.summary: OnProperty evaluates a configured value before a bean or configuration is enabled.

topics.name: Auto-Configuration Files
topics.summary: Find the registration file and follow how Boot discovers configuration candidates.

subTopics.name: Legacy Auto-Configuration Registration in spring.factories (Through Boot 2.7)
subTopics.summary: Older Boot versions used spring.factories under the EnableAutoConfiguration key. Boot 2.7 supported both formats.

subTopics.name: AutoConfiguration.imports (Introduced in Boot 2.7)
subTopics.summary: AutoConfiguration.imports lists candidate classes and is the registration format for Boot 3 and later.

subTopics.name: How auto-config classes are loaded
subTopics.summary: Boot reads candidate names from classpath metadata, then conditions determine what applies.

topics.name: Disable / Customize Auto-Config
topics.summary: Replace one default or opt out of an entire auto-configuration when needed.

subTopics.name: exclude attribute
subTopics.summary: Use the application annotation's exclude setting to skip a specific auto-configuration class.

subTopics.name: spring.autoconfigure.exclude
subTopics.summary: Set spring.autoconfigure.exclude when the exclusions belong in external configuration.

subTopics.name: Overriding auto-configured beans
subTopics.summary: Supply a custom bean when the relevant Boot configuration is designed to back off.

topics.name: Application Startup
topics.summary: Trace launch from environment preparation to a refreshed context and ready application.

subTopics.name: What happens during SpringApplication.run()
subTopics.summary: SpringApplication prepares the environment, creates and refreshes the context, and invokes configured runners.

subTopics.name: Order of execution
subTopics.summary: Read the startup milestones in order and find where configuration, context refresh, and runners fit.

subTopics.name: When beans are created
subTopics.summary: Most regular singleton instances are created during context refresh unless their creation is deferred.

topics.name: Runners
topics.summary: Run startup tasks with the argument format and ordering they need.

subTopics.name: CommandLineRunner vs ApplicationRunner
subTopics.summary: CommandLineRunner receives raw strings. ApplicationRunner receives parsed ApplicationArguments.

subTopics.name: Use cases
subTopics.summary: Use a runner for startup work such as checking required data or running a command-line job.

subTopics.name: Execution order
subTopics.summary: Use Ordered or Order when multiple runners must run in a deliberate order.

topics.name: Embedded Server
topics.summary: Choose a web server, then configure how and where it listens.

subTopics.name: Embedded Tomcat / Jetty / Netty
subTopics.summary: Servlet stacks can use servers such as Tomcat or Jetty. Reactive stacks commonly use Reactor Netty.

subTopics.name: How Boot starts server internally
subTopics.summary: Boot creates the server through its web server factory while initializing the web context.

subTopics.name: How to change port & server type
subTopics.summary: Set server.port for the port and choose server dependencies that match the web stack.

topics.name: Spring JDBC
topics.summary: Execute SQL directly with Spring's JDBC templates and parameter binding.

subTopics.name: JdbcTemplate & NamedParameterJdbcTemplate
subTopics.summary: Use JdbcTemplate for positional parameters or NamedParameterJdbcTemplate for readable named inputs.

topics.name: Spring Data JPA (Hibernate)
topics.summary: Map entities, write repository queries, and inspect how fetching affects the SQL.

subTopics.name: Why repositories don't need implementation
subTopics.summary: Spring Data creates a repository proxy with standard operations and implementations for supported query methods.

subTopics.name: Entity Mapping (@Entity, @Table, @Id, @GeneratedValue)
subTopics.summary: Mark persistent types and identifiers and describe table mappings or key generation as needed.

subTopics.name: Entity scanning
subTopics.summary: Ensure entity packages fall within Boot's scan or define the boundary with EntityScan.

subTopics.name: Auto-DDL (ddl-auto)
subTopics.summary: Use ddl-auto deliberately and prefer reviewed migrations for production schema changes.

subTopics.name: Repositories (CrudRepository, JpaRepository)
subTopics.summary: Choose a repository interface that exposes the persistence operations your application needs.

subTopics.name: CrudRepository vs JpaRepository
subTopics.summary: CrudRepository offers basic operations. JpaRepository adds JPA-oriented methods such as flushing.

subTopics.name: Query Methods (Derived queries, @Query, Native Queries)
subTopics.summary: Use derived methods for simple queries, JPQL for entity queries, and native SQL when needed.

subTopics.name: Derived query method rules
subTopics.summary: Derived names describe filters and ordering using property paths and supported keywords.

subTopics.name: Relationships (OneToOne, OneToMany, ManyToMany)
subTopics.summary: Define ownership and cardinality explicitly so updates and fetches behave as intended.

subTopics.name: Lazy vs Eager loading
subTopics.summary: Fetching controls when related data is loaded. Confirm the effect on SQL and data size.

subTopics.name: Pagination & Sorting
subTopics.summary: Use a pageable and stable sort. Choose Page or Slice based on whether callers need totals.

subTopics.name: N+1 Problem - What it is
subTopics.summary: N+1 means fetching a list triggers a separate associated-data query for each item.

subTopics.name: N+1 Problem - How to identify
subTopics.summary: Look for repeated SQL statements with different identifiers in a query trace.

subTopics.name: N+1 Problem - Solutions (fetch join, EntityGraph)
subTopics.summary: Fetch needed data deliberately with a fetch join, an entity graph, or a suitable projection.

topics.name: Transaction Management (INTERVIEW FAVORITE)
topics.summary: Keep transaction decisions at clear service boundaries and test rollback behavior.

subTopics.name: @Transactional - How it works internally
subTopics.summary: An eligible proxy call applies transaction configuration before invoking the target method.

subTopics.name: Why @Transactional uses AOP
subTopics.summary: Transaction advice handles setup and completion around a method call that crosses the proxy.

subTopics.name: Propagation types (REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW)
subTopics.summary: Required joins or starts work. RequiresNew starts a separate transaction.

subTopics.name: Isolation levels
subTopics.summary: Isolation controls what concurrent transactions can see. Available behavior depends on the database.

subTopics.name: Rollback Rules - Checked vs Runtime exception
subTopics.summary: Unchecked exceptions and errors default to rollback in typical Spring configuration. Checked failures need a rule when appropriate.

subTopics.name: How to force rollback
subTopics.summary: Throw an exception covered by rollback rules or mark the active transaction rollback-only when needed.

subTopics.name: Common Pitfalls - Why @Transactional doesn't work on private methods
subTopics.summary: A private method is not an eligible entry point for ordinary transactional proxies.

subTopics.name: Common Pitfalls - Why @Transactional doesn't work on internal method calls
subTopics.summary: Self-invocation bypasses the proxy. Put the transaction boundary where another bean calls it.

subTopics.name: Proxy limitation explanation
subTopics.summary: A proxy intercepts eligible external calls. The invocation path matters as much as the annotation.

topics.name: NoSQL Integration
topics.summary: Choose a document or in-memory data store for the access pattern you need.

subTopics.name: Spring Data MongoDB
subTopics.summary: Map Java objects to MongoDB documents and query them through Spring Data.

subTopics.name: Spring Data Redis (Caching & Pub/Sub)
subTopics.summary: Use Redis for expiring cached values or publish/subscribe, with explicit serialization and expiry choices.

topics.name: Database Migration
topics.summary: Track database changes as reviewed migrations that can run consistently across environments.

subTopics.name: Flyway or Liquibase integration
subTopics.summary: Flyway and Liquibase record which migrations were applied and help reproduce the database schema.

topics.name: Controllers
topics.summary: Map HTTP requests to clear controller methods with explicit input sources.

subTopics.name: @RestController vs @Controller
subTopics.summary: RestController defaults to writing response bodies. Controller can return views when configured for MVC.

subTopics.name: @RequestMapping vs @GetMapping
subTopics.summary: Use RequestMapping for general mapping and GetMapping for a GET-only handler.

subTopics.name: @PathVariable vs @RequestParam
subTopics.summary: PathVariable reads the route segment. RequestParam reads a named request parameter.

subTopics.name: @RequestBody vs @ModelAttribute
subTopics.summary: Bind serialized payloads with RequestBody and bind request parameters to objects with ModelAttribute.

topics.name: Response Handling
topics.summary: Make response status, headers, and body reflect the operation's outcome.

subTopics.name: ResponseEntity
subTopics.summary: Use ResponseEntity when a handler needs explicit control over body, headers, or status.

subTopics.name: HTTP status codes best practices
subTopics.summary: Choose HTTP status by outcome, such as 201 for creation or 404 for a missing resource.

topics.name: Exception Handling
topics.summary: Return predictable error responses from local or shared handlers.

subTopics.name: @ExceptionHandler
subTopics.summary: Use ExceptionHandler to map an exception to a safe response body and status.

subTopics.name: @ControllerAdvice
subTopics.summary: Use ControllerAdvice to reuse exception handlers across controllers.

subTopics.name: Global vs local exception handling
subTopics.summary: Handle endpoint-specific cases locally and centralize shared error formats and mappings.

topics.name: Advanced REST
topics.summary: Validate inputs, negotiate representations, and handle binary data deliberately.

subTopics.name: Bean Validation (Hibernate Validator, @Valid, @NotNull, @Size)
subTopics.summary: Use Valid to trigger validation for incoming data and constraints to describe what is accepted.

subTopics.name: HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State)
subTopics.summary: Include links that expose useful related resources and actions to API clients.

subTopics.name: Content Negotiation (JSON vs XML)
subTopics.summary: Use Accept to negotiate response representations and Content-Type to describe the submitted payload.

subTopics.name: File Upload/Download
subTopics.summary: Use multipart handling for uploads and appropriate media types and headers for downloads.

topics.name: API Documentation
topics.summary: Describe API operations and schemas so clients can discover how to call them.

subTopics.name: OpenAPI 3.0 / Swagger (SpringDoc)
subTopics.summary: SpringDoc can generate an OpenAPI document and expose an interactive Swagger UI.

topics.name: Core Concepts
topics.summary: Follow a request through identity checks and permission decisions.

subTopics.name: Authentication vs Authorization
subTopics.summary: Authentication identifies the caller. Authorization determines which actions that identity may perform.

subTopics.name: Stateless vs Stateful auth
subTopics.summary: Sessions retain authentication state on the server. Stateless requests carry their credentials each time.

subTopics.name: SecurityFilterChain
subTopics.summary: A SecurityFilterChain applies configured security filters to matching requests.

topics.name: JWT with Spring Boot
topics.summary: Trace a bearer token from the incoming header through validation to a security context.

subTopics.name: Why JWT is stateless
subTopics.summary: A signed token can carry claims with each request, allowing authentication without a server-side login session.

subTopics.name: Filter flow
subTopics.summary: A bearer filter reads the token and passes it to authentication before authorization runs.

subTopics.name: Where token is validated
subTopics.summary: The configured decoder or provider verifies the signature and expected token claims before accepting identity.

topics.name: Method Security
topics.summary: Apply permissions before a method runs or after its return value is available.

subTopics.name: @PreAuthorize
subTopics.summary: PreAuthorize evaluates a permission expression before invoking an eligible method.

subTopics.name: @PostAuthorize
subTopics.summary: PostAuthorize can check the returned value before it is delivered to the caller.

subTopics.name: Role vs Authority
subTopics.summary: Authorities are permission strings. Roles commonly group privileges under a role prefix.

topics.name: CSRF & CORS
topics.summary: Choose cross-origin and CSRF policies based on browser behavior and credential handling.

subTopics.name: What CSRF is
subTopics.summary: CSRF can trigger an unintended action when the browser automatically includes an authenticated user's credentials.

subTopics.name: When REST APIs Need CSRF Protection
subTopics.summary: An API using only explicit bearer headers has different exposure from one using cookies. Assess its credential flow before disabling protection.

subTopics.name: Browser-side vs server-side CORS
subTopics.summary: The server advertises allowed origins and methods. Browsers enforce that policy across origins.

topics.name: Service Discovery
topics.summary: Discover service instances dynamically as their addresses change.

subTopics.name: Netflix Eureka / HashiCorp Consul
subTopics.summary: Eureka or Consul can provide a registry that clients use to find available service instances.

topics.name: API Gateway
topics.summary: Centralize route selection and common request policies at the edge.

subTopics.name: Spring Cloud Gateway (Routing, Filtering, Rate Limiting)
subTopics.summary: Spring Cloud Gateway matches routes and applies filters, such as rate limits, before forwarding requests.

topics.name: Config Management
topics.summary: Serve application configuration from a central source while keeping secrets protected.

subTopics.name: Spring Cloud Config Server (Centralized configuration)
subTopics.summary: Config Server can expose shared, versioned settings to application clients.

topics.name: Resilience & Fault Tolerance
topics.summary: Choose resilience controls that match a failure mode and keep retries bounded.

subTopics.name: Resilience4j (Circuit Breaker, Retry, Rate Limiter, Bulkhead)
subTopics.summary: Use a circuit breaker to stop repeated failures, a retry for transient errors, and a bulkhead to isolate capacity.

topics.name: Distributed Tracing
topics.summary: Follow one request across services by propagating trace context.

subTopics.name: Micrometer Tracing (formerly Sleuth) + Zipkin/Brave
subTopics.summary: Micrometer Tracing records spans and can export them using compatible systems such as Zipkin.

topics.name: Introduction to Generative AI
topics.summary: Understand what a language model can do and where application checks are still needed.

subTopics.name: Large Language Models (LLMs) concepts
subTopics.summary: LLMs predict tokens from context. Evaluate output for accuracy, relevance, and consistency.

topics.name: Spring AI Core
topics.summary: Send prompts through a Java client and turn responses into data your application can check.

subTopics.name: Chat Client API: Interacting with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, HuggingFace
subTopics.summary: ChatClient gives Java code a fluent interface for requesting model responses across configured integrations.

subTopics.name: Prompts: Prompt Templates, Prompt Engineering within Java
subTopics.summary: Use templates to separate reusable instructions from request-specific values.

subTopics.name: Output Parsers: Converting AI text responses into Java Objects (POJOs)
subTopics.summary: Convert structured model output into Java objects and validate it before using it.

topics.name: Embeddings & Vector Databases
topics.summary: Represent text as vectors and retrieve material related to a query.

subTopics.name: Text Embeddings models
subTopics.summary: An embedding model represents text as numeric vectors that support similarity comparisons.

subTopics.name: Vector Store integration (PGVector, Pinecone, Milvus, Redis)
subTopics.summary: Store vectors with source metadata and choose an integration that fits query and filtering requirements.

topics.name: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)
topics.summary: Retrieve source material before generating an answer so the model has relevant context.

subTopics.name: Document Readers (PDF, Text, JSON)
subTopics.summary: Load documents into a consistent representation with source metadata before indexing them.

subTopics.name: Token Splitters
subTopics.summary: Split text into chunks that conserve context while fitting model and retrieval limits.

subTopics.name: Contextual search implementation
subTopics.summary: Retrieve relevant chunks for the question and include them in the prompt with useful source context.

topics.name: Advanced AI
topics.summary: Connect models to application tools or image services for tasks beyond text generation.

subTopics.name: Function Calling (Letting AI call your Java methods)
subTopics.summary: Register a tool with a clear input contract and validate arguments before invoking a Java method.

subTopics.name: Image Generation (DALL-E, Stability AI)
subTopics.summary: Use an image generation integration to submit prompts and handle the returned image data.

topics.name: JMS (Java Message Service)
topics.summary: Send messages through the standard Jakarta Messaging API and choose durable delivery as needed.

subTopics.name: ActiveMQ integration
subTopics.summary: Configure a JMS-compatible broker such as ActiveMQ and use Spring abstractions to send or receive messages.

topics.name: Apache Kafka
topics.summary: Publish and process records with Kafka's partitions and consumer groups.

subTopics.name: Spring for Apache Kafka
subTopics.summary: Spring for Apache Kafka provides templates and listener containers for common producer and consumer tasks.

subTopics.name: Producers, Consumers, Consumer Groups
subTopics.summary: Producers write records, consumers read them, and group members share partitions.

topics.name: RabbitMQ
topics.summary: Route messages to RabbitMQ queues using exchange types and routing keys.

subTopics.name: Exchanges, Queues, Routing Keys
subTopics.summary: Publish to an exchange, then use bindings and routing keys to decide which queues receive the message.

topics.name: Spring Cloud Stream
topics.summary: Keep application message handlers separate from the broker integration they use.

subTopics.name: Binder abstraction (Switch between Kafka/RabbitMQ easily)
subTopics.summary: A binder connects functions to a broker. Broker-specific delivery and ordering guarantees still need review.

topics.name: Scheduling
topics.summary: Schedule periodic work and choose a scheduler based on durability and coordination needs.

subTopics.name: @Scheduled (FixedRate, FixedDelay, Cron expressions)
subTopics.summary: FixedRate measures between start times, FixedDelay waits after completion, and cron follows a calendar schedule.

subTopics.name: Quartz Scheduler integration
subTopics.summary: Use Quartz for more involved schedules and configured persistent job state.

topics.name: Spring Batch
topics.summary: Process large inputs with restartable jobs, explicit chunks, and measured concurrency.

subTopics.name: Job, Step, JobRepository
subTopics.summary: A Job contains steps, and the JobRepository records execution metadata and restart state.

subTopics.name: ItemReader, ItemProcessor, ItemWriter
subTopics.summary: Read items, optionally transform them, and write the results through three focused contracts.

subTopics.name: Chunk-oriented processing
subTopics.summary: Process and write batches of items within transaction boundaries sized for the workload.

subTopics.name: Error handling (Skip, Retry policies)
subTopics.summary: Retry transient failures and skip selected bad items when the job's rules allow it.

subTopics.name: Parallel processing & Partitioning
subTopics.summary: Partition work into independent units and check whether shared components are safe to use concurrently.

topics.name: Project Reactor
topics.summary: Build reactive pipelines that handle both results and demand.

subTopics.name: Mono vs Flux
subTopics.summary: Mono has zero or one item. Flux can emit zero or many items.

subTopics.name: Backpressure
subTopics.summary: Backpressure lets a subscriber signal how many items it is ready to receive.

topics.name: Spring WebFlux
topics.summary: Keep a reactive request path non-blocking from HTTP through database access.

subTopics.name: Non-blocking REST APIs
subTopics.summary: Compose asynchronous publishers for HTTP handlers and avoid blocking calls on event-loop threads.

subTopics.name: Netty Server
subTopics.summary: Reactor Netty uses event loops to handle network I/O for many concurrent connections.

subTopics.name: Reactive Database Access (R2DBC)
subTopics.summary: Use an R2DBC driver and compatible access APIs for reactive relational database operations.

topics.name: Testing Types
topics.summary: Choose the smallest test scope that proves the behavior you care about.

subTopics.name: Unit vs Integration testing
subTopics.summary: Unit tests check an isolated behavior. Integration tests check how the real pieces work together.

topics.name: Unit Testing
topics.summary: Test a class's behavior with explicit inputs, assertions, and focused test doubles.

subTopics.name: JUnit 5 & Mockito (Mocking dependencies)
subTopics.summary: Use JUnit assertions for outcomes and Mockito when a real dependency would obscure the test.

topics.name: Integration Testing
topics.summary: Load the full context or a smaller test slice, depending on the boundary you need to prove.

subTopics.name: @SpringBootTest
subTopics.summary: SpringBootTest loads the application context for integration tests and can start a server when configured.

subTopics.name: Test Slices (@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest)
subTopics.summary: WebMvcTest focuses on the web layer. DataJpaTest focuses on JPA components.

topics.name: Mocking
topics.summary: Replace or observe collaborators selectively so tests stay clear.

subTopics.name: Mockito basics
subTopics.summary: Stub a result to set up a scenario, then verify interactions only when they are part of the contract.

subTopics.name: MockBean vs SpyBean
subTopics.summary: A mock replaces behavior. A spy wraps a real instance. In newer Spring tests, use MockitoBean or MockitoSpyBean.

topics.name: Advanced Testing
topics.summary: Exercise external boundaries with disposable services or predictable HTTP responses.

subTopics.name: Testcontainers (Spinning up real DBs/Kafka in Docker for tests)
subTopics.summary: Testcontainers starts disposable dependencies so tests can exercise real drivers and protocols.

subTopics.name: WireMock (Mocking external APIs)
subTopics.summary: WireMock serves controlled HTTP responses for tests of clients and error handling.

topics.name: Spring Boot Actuator
topics.summary: Use operational endpoints to inspect application health and metrics safely.

subTopics.name: Important endpoints: /health, /metrics, /info
subTopics.summary: Check health for status, metrics for measurements, and info for published metadata.

subTopics.name: Custom health indicators
subTopics.summary: A custom HealthIndicator reports dependency status with details appropriate for the endpoint's audience.

topics.name: Monitoring
topics.summary: Collect application measurements and turn them into observable trends.

subTopics.name: Micrometer basics
subTopics.summary: Micrometer provides APIs for counters, timers, and gauges with tags.

subTopics.name: Prometheus & Grafana overview
subTopics.summary: Prometheus collects metrics and Grafana can graph and alert on their trends.

topics.name: Logging
topics.summary: Produce consistent application logs and make them searchable across instances.

subTopics.name: SLF4J, Logback
subTopics.summary: SLF4J is a logging facade. Logback is one implementation that formats and writes events.

subTopics.name: Log aggregation (ELK Stack: Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana)
subTopics.summary: Aggregate application logs in a searchable store and attach enough context to investigate incidents.

topics.name: Deployment
topics.summary: Package the application and its dependencies for repeatable deployment.

subTopics.name: Dockerizing Spring Boot
subTopics.summary: Build a container image, externalize its configuration, and use appropriate health checks.

subTopics.name: Why Boot apps are container-friendly
subTopics.summary: An executable package can launch with a standard Java command and accept deployment-specific settings.

subTopics.name: Fat JAR vs Thin JAR
subTopics.summary: An executable fat JAR packages its dependencies. A thin JAR needs them supplied separately.

topics.name: Startup & Memory
topics.summary: Measure where startup time and memory go before changing packaging or initialization.

subTopics.name: Why Spring Boot apps are heavy
subTopics.summary: Dependencies, caches, initialized beans, and runtime settings can all contribute to resource use.

subTopics.name: Reduce startup time
subTopics.summary: Profile startup, then remove unused configuration or selectively defer expensive work.

subTopics.name: GraalVM Native Image (concept)
subTopics.summary: Native Image compiles an application ahead of time and has a different runtime and deployment model.

subTopics.name: Native Images: Startup and Compatibility Trade-offs
subTopics.summary: Compare lower startup or memory costs against build time and compatibility constraints using your workload.

topics.name: Common Production Issues
topics.summary: Diagnose common failures by checking bean names, dependency graphs, and effective configuration.

subTopics.name: Bean overriding issues
subTopics.summary: Find duplicate bean names and choose explicit names or registrations instead of masking collisions.

subTopics.name: Circular dependencies
subTopics.summary: Review dependency cycles and split responsibilities when two services depend directly on each other.

subTopics.name: Configuration mismatch across environments
subTopics.summary: Compare resolved properties, active profiles, and external overrides between environments.

topics.name: GraphQL
topics.summary: Expose a typed API whose queries select the fields they need.

subTopics.name: Spring for GraphQL (Controller, Schema, DataFetchers)
subTopics.summary: Define a schema and map query fields to controller or data-fetching methods.

topics.name: WebSockets
topics.summary: Send live updates over a persistent connection and choose a messaging protocol when useful.

subTopics.name: STOMP protocol, SockJS, Real-time chat
subTopics.summary: STOMP adds messaging conventions, and SockJS can provide fallback transports for supported clients.

topics.name: Caching
topics.summary: Cache repeatable results and decide how entries are invalidated.

subTopics.name: @Cacheable, @CacheEvict
subTopics.summary: Cacheable can reuse a prior result. CacheEvict removes entries when the underlying data changes.

subTopics.name: Providers: Caffeine, Redis
subTopics.summary: Use Caffeine for an in-process cache or Redis for shared cache storage across instances.
